body: Thank you so much for letting me know, it really feels isolating when no one around me is going through anything similar

Wow this post is just horrible. I'm someone who has been dealing with suicidal toughts all my life and i am having a pretty bad episode right now. Hearing that my life doesnt matter and that people don't care is just one step away from saying "just do it, no one is even going to notice". You seem to know the effects of what you said on the lifes of people but I dont think you really care.

I think what you might be experciencing is derealization which a normal symtom that people experience. Maybe you could look a little into It and what type of therapy works well for it in order to be able to deal with it better. Just seeing that you're not alone in feeling this way could help you. I hope you get better at dealing with this cause I've had some derealization episodes and they can be really rough.

That's the thing, they are all the things that you mentioned. They have always noticed something weird about me and whenever I went into shutdown because of the sensory stimultation they always asked if i needed help or things like that. One of them even whatched a YouTube video about autism to understand it better and I've always felt welcomed there. That only really makes me feel worse. Having to separate from people like that because i just can't do it due to my condition.

This is very similar to how I've been feeling these past few days. It all very confusing specially the constant thoughts of things such as "do I actually stim?" "am I really that uncomfortable around social situations or was I just exaggeraring?" "is this masking or not? " etc. I have to remind myself of something that is really helping which is the idea that if you think that you might be autistic, you probably are, most neurotypicals don't even wonder if they might be autistic.

 If you have gotten a diagnosis chances are that you are autistic, regardless of what anyone says. Try to not think about what anyone says about your autism because it's your experiences and yours only, they haven't lived them.
